brief.headline: Chemco sits in the Altman grey zone (Z=2.17) — lead with supply security and a second source, then trade faster payment (worth 12.19% to them) for a 6-8% price cut.

priceAsk.summary: Request a 6-8% price reduction in exchange for faster payment and committed volume.
priceAsk.target: A discount worth approximately their borrowing cost of 12.19%, split between faster cash and volume commitment.
priceAsk.basis: Chemco earns a 5.9% net margin vs the peer median of 3.8% — there is 2.1 points of headroom. Their cash cycle of 104d runs 25 days longer than the peer median of 79d, so early payment has real value. They are growing at 22.1%/yr and need volume.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 30 Days After Receipt to immediate payment or 15 days, in exchange for price.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to net-15 frees ₹22.57 L of their working capital; moving to immediate frees ₹45.14 L.

brief.financialLeverage: Chemco posted ₹937.60 Cr revenue in FY2024-25 with a 5.9% net margin, 2.1 points above the peer median of 3.8%, and a 16.1% EBITDA margin. Their return on capital of 16.3% beats the peer median of 14.9%. Debt-to-equity stands at 0.83x with interest coverage of 2.94x, and they hold a CRISIL A+ / Stable rating. However, their Altman Z-score of 2.17 puts them in the grey zone — not distressed, but not robust. Our ₹5.49 Cr spend is only 0.59% of their revenue, so we have limited spend leverage. Given the grey-zone signal, frame the negotiation around qualifying Manjushree Technopack as a second source (they are India's largest rigid-plastic converter at ₹2569.83 Cr) to manage continuity risk, then offer commercial upside — faster payment and volume — in return for a meaningful price cut. Do not squeeze so hard that you destabilise a supplier already showing stress flags.

evidence.point: Chemco's net margin of 5.9% is 2.1 percentage points fatter than the peer median
Their cash-conversion cycle runs 25 days longer than peers, so they value faster cash
They pay their own suppliers 12 days slower than the peer median, so extending our terms is only fair
Chemco's borrowing cost sits at 12.19%, so paying them 15 or 30 days early is worth roughly that rate in interest savings
Their Altman Z-score of 2.17 places them in the grey zone, signalling elevated financial stress
Chemco is growing revenue at 22.1% per year, so committed volume has strategic value to them

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, with pharma bottles, caps and preforms capability — the top second-source candidate (Health: B 65/100).

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader at ₹946.50 Cr revenue, serving pharma with pails and containers — a robust, profitable alternate (Health: B 73/100).

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed player with ₹701.17 Cr revenue in moulded and blow-moulded packaging, covering bottles and caps (Health: C 51/100).

risks: Altman Z of 2.17 puts Chemco in the grey zone — push too hard and you may tip a fragile supplier into real distress, creating a continuity problem.
Our ₹5.49 Cr spend is only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue, so we lack spend weight — frame the ask around supply risk and commercial opportunity, not volume threat.

The CRISIL A+ rating and 2.94x interest coverage suggest they are still serviceable, but the Probe42 score of 4/10 and grey-zone Altman signal warrant caution — prioritise qualifying Manjushree as a live second source before pressing hard.
They already stretch payables to 49d vs the peer 37d, so asking for even longer terms (beyond current 30d) may meet resistance unless paired with volume or price upside for them.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're qualifying Manjushree Technopack as a second source for continuity, but we'd rather grow with you — let's talk about faster payment and committed volume in exchange for a sharper price.
